news.exam_corner_topic: Australian MP 'full of gratitude' upon leaving hospital after alleged car attack
news.headline: Australian MP 'full of gratitude' upon leaving hospital after alleged car attack
news.story_lead: Independent MP Helen Haines has been released from hospital after an alleged attack last month - Published 16 November 2026, 01:53 GMT Australian politician Helen Haines has said she is "full of gratitude" upon being discharged from hospital, four weeks after she was allegedly attacked with a car and left a double amputee. The independent MP was struck outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, north-east of Melbourne, on October 19, an incident which horrified Australia. Brendan Nugent, 43, has been charged with dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury and the federal offence of causing harm to a public official.
news.full_article_text: Independent MP Helen Haines has been released from hospital after an alleged attack last month - Published 16 November 2026, 01:53 GMT Australian politician Helen Haines has said she is "full of gratitude" upon being discharged from hospital, four weeks after she was allegedly attacked with a car and left a double amputee. The independent MP was struck outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, north-east of Melbourne, on October 19, an incident which horrified Australia. Brendan Nugent, 43, has been charged with dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury and the federal offence of causing harm to a public official. He has yet to enter pleas. In her first public comments since the attack, Haines, 65, said she had moved into the rehabilitation stage of her recovery. "This is a really positive moment, and I am full of gratitude for the expert and compassionate care I received at the Alfred and am receiving in this next stage," Haines said. "I appreciate the thousands of warm wishes and supportive messages from people across Indi, throughout Australia and around the world. They are giving me strength as I focus on this next phase of healing." She added that she had been "overwhelmed" by the generosity of well wishers who had donated to Save the Children in her honour. Haines, known for supporting stronger climate action and helping establish a national anti-corruption commission, entered parliament in 2019 as the Member for Indi after working as a nurse and midwife. Victoria Police has said its investigation, with support from the Australian Federal Police, remains ongoing and a motive is yet to be established. Nugent's father said he and his wife had been long-time friends of Haines, and Nugent's lawyer has said his client has mental health concerns. The incident sparked a reckoning in the country more broadly over the tone of public debate. Though a motive is still unclear, politicians, law enforcement, and experts have said heated public discourse is heightening the threat of political violence in the country. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said he had been in regular contact with Haines and her "extraordinary" family. "All our thoughts and prayers continue to be with Helen for her recovery," he said in a statement. "We continue to provide support to Helen, her family, community and staff as she undertakes her rehabilitation." news.headline: ‘Inappropriate to interfere in internal debate’: Italian legislator slams European socialist leader over ‘vote thieves' remark targeting BJP
news.story_lead: ‘Inappropriate to interfere in internal debate’: Italian legislator slams European socialist leader over ‘vote thieves' remark targeting BJP Her remarks came after Giacomo Filibeck described Indian democracy as being "under attack" and voiced support for Congress leader Rahul Gandhi. Italian legislator Deborah Bergamini on Monday criticised European socialist leader Giacomo Filibeck over his "vote thieves, step down" remark targeting the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), saying India has its own political institutions and judiciary to resolve domestic political disputes. “I believe everyone in a democracy is free to put forward whatever arguments and accusations they wish, provided they can substantiate them,' she said in a Facebook post.
news.full_article_text: ‘Inappropriate to interfere in internal debate’: Italian legislator slams European socialist leader over ‘vote thieves' remark targeting BJP Her remarks came after Giacomo Filibeck described Indian democracy as being "under attack" and voiced support for Congress leader Rahul Gandhi. Italian legislator Deborah Bergamini on Monday criticised European socialist leader Giacomo Filibeck over his "vote thieves, step down" remark targeting the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), saying India has its own political institutions and judiciary to resolve domestic political disputes. “I believe everyone in a democracy is free to put forward whatever arguments and accusations they wish, provided they can substantiate them,' she said in a Facebook post. Her remarks came after Filibeck, the Secretary General of the Party of European Socialists (PES), described Indian democracy as being "under attack" and voiced support for Congress leader and Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi. Speaking to news agency ANI on the sidelines of the Bharat Summit 2026, organised by the Congress in Hyderabad, Filibeck said international gatherings were important to draw global attention to challenges concerning democracy in India. "Democracy is under attack in India, and we need to defend it, and the best way to defend it is to stand by Rahul Gandhi and the Indian Congress Party," he said. Filibeck also said the PES, the Congress and other political movements across the world were part of a progressive alliance committed to social justice, climate justice, human rights and democracy, according to ANI. Bergamini hails India-Italy ties Bergamini also stressed the close ties between India and Italy, saying it was inappropriate to interfere in the domestic political affairs of a friendly country with which Italy has a special strategic partnership and extensive cooperation across various sectors. “Moreover, in cases like this, it is inappropriate to interfere in the domestic political debate of a major friendly country with which our nation has established a special strategic partnership, developing close cooperation across all sectors,” she added. She questioned the appropriateness of European representatives lecturing India on democracy, pointing to the country's large electorate. "Moreover, as Europeans, we find it inappropriate to lecture on democracy a nation that enables 970 million citizens to cast their votes. India possesses its own political institutions and judiciary; any conflicts or disputes should be addressed and resolved in accordance with the established rules of democracy," she added. BJP slams Rahul Gandhi Union minister Kiren Rijiju on Sunday took a veiled dig at Congress leaders, including Gandhi, after Filibeck raised the slogan "Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod" at the Congress's Bharat Summit 2026 in Hyderabad. "Have you ever seen anyone laughing when India is insulted by a foreigner? I'm not asking about which Indian goes abroad to insult India," Rijiju said in a post on X, without naming anyone. Rahul Gandhi and Telangana chief minister Revanth Reddy were seen laughing and applauding in a widely circulated video of Filibeck raising the slogan, which was in reference to the ongoing controversy over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. BJP national spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari also accused Rahul Gandhi of seeking foreign interference in India's domestic political affairs. In a post on X, Bhandari alleged that Gandhi had become a "puppet of foreign powers & George Soros wanting instability in India". "Rahul Gandhi wants Regime Change with Foreign help," he said, claiming that the Congress leader's interactions with foreign delegates reflected an attempt to seek international support to remove the government led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Meanwhile, Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut defended Filibeck's remarks and questioned the BJP's criticism of the Italian politician. "If Modi can offer Melody chocolates to the Italian Prime Minister, then an Italian politician can come here and speak about this country. Democracy is being murdered in the country; this is a UN and human rights issue, not a matter involving any foreign power," Raut said. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR HT News Desk Follow the latest breaking news, major developments and agenda-setting stories from India and around the world with the newsdesk at Hindustan Times. news.headline: Sabarimala temple to open for annual pilgrimage; AI cameras part of crowd management
news.story_lead: Sabarimala temple to open for annual pilgrimage; AI cameras part of crowd management While the pilgrimage season formally begins Tuesday, which marks the first day of the Malayalam month of Vrischikam, the temple doors will open to pilgrims on Monday evening itself The sanctum sanctorum of the Sabarimala temple will open on Monday ahead of the annual Mandalam - Makaravilakku pilgrimage season, which begins on November 17. While the pilgrimage season formally begins Tuesday, which marks the first day of the Malayalam month of Vrischikam, the temple doors will open to pilgrims on Monday evening itself. Temple affairs minister K Muraleedharan said a new crowd management system has been put in place that will allow up to 75 pilgrims to climb the 18 holy steps leading to the shrine in a minute.
news.full_article_text: Sabarimala temple to open for annual pilgrimage; AI cameras part of crowd management While the pilgrimage season formally begins Tuesday, which marks the first day of the Malayalam month of Vrischikam, the temple doors will open to pilgrims on Monday evening itself The sanctum sanctorum of the Sabarimala temple will open on Monday ahead of the annual Mandalam - Makaravilakku pilgrimage season, which begins on November 17. While the pilgrimage season formally begins Tuesday, which marks the first day of the Malayalam month of Vrischikam, the temple doors will open to pilgrims on Monday evening itself. Temple affairs minister K Muraleedharan said a new crowd management system has been put in place that will allow up to 75 pilgrims to climb the 18 holy steps leading to the shrine in a minute. The narrow and steep steps is where a gridlock occurs in crowd management especially during the pilgrimage season. Also Read: Sabarimala women entry issue resurfaces over reported claims by ex-TDB chief The minister said the police and security staff of the Travancore Devaswom Board (TDB), which oversees the temple, have been instructed to ensure smooth management of crowds. ADGP (law and order) P Vijayan told media persons that cameras equipped with AI features have been installed as part of security and to boost crowd management. Footfall data from previous pilgrimage seasons have been analysed to prepare for peak arrival timings of devotees. Two large sheds, to accommodate around 6,000 pilgrims at a time, have been erected, he said. Also Read: Nine-judge SC bench reserves verdict in Sabarimala reference Instructions have been issued to the health department to ensure adequate stock of medicines at health centres at the hill shrine. For the first time, the TDB has tied up with Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) for a pilgrim insurance scheme as part of which a compensation of ₹ 2 lakh is offered in the case of a pilgrim’s death during the pilgrimage. Devotees who book slots through the virtual queue and spot booking systems will get the insurance cover. The TDB will cover the annual premium of ₹ 1.5 crore.

news.headline: Supreme Court Proposes Financial Compensation for Crime Victims' Families Even Upon Acquittal of Accused
news.story_lead: The Supreme Court of India proposed that families of murder victims should be considered for financial compensation under state victim protection schemes even when the accused is acquitted due to lack of evidence beyond reasonable doubt. A bench comprising Justices Satish Chandra Sharma and N. Kotiswar Singh highlighted that the loss endured by a victim's family must not go unaddressed merely because a criminal charge could not be proved.
news.full_article_text:
### Supreme Court Advocates Victim Compensation Beyond Conviction
The Supreme Court of India suggested that victim compensation schemes should cover cases where criminal trials result in an acquittal due to the prosecution's failure to establish guilt beyond a reasonable doubt. A bench consisting of Justice Satish Chandra Sharma and Justice N. Kotiswar Singh made this observation while acquitting an accused in a 2011 double-murder case from Haryana. The bench instructed the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) in Bhiwani to review the relevant provisions of the victim compensation framework and examine whether financial assistance can be provided to the families of the two deceased women.

### Context of the 2011 Haryana Murder Case
The case relates to the murder of two widowed women, Shakuntala and Suman, on April 17, 2011, in Ranila village within Haryana's Bhiwani district. According to the prosecution, the victims were publicly beaten to death with sticks by their nephew Naresh and another individual named Subhash over disputes regarding personal relationships. Following their arrest two days after the crime, a fast-track court in Bhiwani convicted Naresh in 2013 and awarded him the death penalty.

### Acquittal and Directions to Legal Services Authority
Upon reviewing the appeal, the Supreme Court determined that the prosecution had failed to establish the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt, leading to Naresh's acquittal. However, recognizing that the acquitted outcome leaves the victims' families without justice or financial relief, the court directed the Bhiwani DLSA to explore state assistance mechanisms. The decision relies on the victim compensation framework under Section 357A of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), which has been substantially carried forward under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).

Under Section 357A, state governments, in consultation with the Central Government, are required to formulate schemes providing financial compensation to victims or their dependants who suffer loss or injury from crime and require rehabilitation. Crucially, the law empowers courts to recommend compensation even in instances ending in acquittal or discharge if the victim or their dependants require rehabilitation.
news.background_context: The case stems from an April 17, 2011 incident in Ranila village, Bhiwani district, Haryana, where two widowed women were killed. In 2013, a local fast-track court sentenced the accused to death. The matter reached the Supreme Court on appeal, where the conviction was overturned due to insufficient prosecution evidence.

A bench of Justices Satish Chandra Sharma and N. Kotiswar Singh issued the direction while acquitting an accused in a 2011 Haryana double-murder case.
The court directed the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) in Bhiwani to evaluate victim compensation options for the families.
The incident occurred on April 17, 2011, in Ranila village, Bhiwani district, resulting in the death of two widowed women, Shakuntala and Suman.
In 2013, a fast-track court in Bhiwani had awarded the death sentence to the accused, Naresh.
The Supreme Court acquitted the accused because the prosecution failed to prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt.
The proposal relies on Section 357A of the CrPC, which is now carried forward under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).
Section 357A permits compensation recommendations even when proceedings end in acquittal or discharge if rehabilitation is required.

Location of Crime: Ranila village, Bhiwani district, Haryana.
Date of Crime: April 17, 2011.
Victims: Shakuntala and Suman (widowed women).
Accused Acquitted: Naresh (sentenced to death by fast-track court in 2013).
Statutory Provision: Section 357A of CrPC / Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).
Implementing Agency: District Legal Services Authority (DLSA), Bhiwani.

2013: Fast-track court in Bhiwani sentences accused Naresh to death

exam_relevance: GS Paper II (Polity & Governance): Criminal justice reform, victim rights, role of Legal Services Authorities, and statutory provisions under CrPC/BNSS.
Prelims: Section 357A CrPC/BNSS provisions, functions of District Legal Services Authority (DLSA), Legal Services Authorities Act 1987.
news.upsc_analysis: The Supreme Court's proposal highlights a critical gap in India's criminal justice system, where legal outcomes focus primarily on convicting the accused rather than restoring the victim. By linking victim compensation to the harm suffered rather than the outcome of trial (conviction vs acquittal), the court reinforces the principle of state responsibility in victim rehabilitation under Section 357A CrPC / BNSS.
causes: Failure of the prosecution to establish guilt beyond reasonable doubt led to the acquittal of the accused.
Absence of automatic financial compensation for crime victims when trials end in acquittals.
impacts: Strengthens victim-centric jurisprudence in Indian criminal law.
Ensures that dependants of victims receive rehabilitation support regardless of conviction outcomes.
Activates the role of District Legal Services Authorities in post-trial victim assessment.
challenges: Resource constraints and delays in processing compensation through state legal service authorities.
Varying state-level implementation standards for victim compensation schemes under Section 357A CrPC / BNSS.
government_steps: Enactment of Section 357A under CrPC (and its retention under BNSS) enabling court-directed victim compensation schemes.
Establishment of District Legal Services Authorities to assess and distribute victim assistance funds.
constitutional_or_policy_link: Section 357A of Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) / Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)
way_forward: State governments should streamline victim compensation funds to ensure prompt disbursement without awaiting final appellate outcomes.
DLSAs must proactively evaluate victim requirements immediately following trial conclusions, irrespective of conviction or acquittal.
news.mains_notes:
### Victim-Centric Justice System
- Traditional criminal jurisprudence focuses primarily on penalising the offender.
- Section 357A CrPC (now under BNSS) shifts focus towards victim rehabilitation.

### SC Directive Key Takeaways
- Loss of life or trauma suffered by victims/dependants exists independently of whether prosecution secures a conviction.
- Acquittal due to lack of evidence beyond reasonable doubt should not deprive dependants of state-backed rehabilitation.
- Institutional mechanism: DLSAs play the primary role in assessing financial need and disbursing funds.

prelims_facts: Section 357A of CrPC allows compensation to victims or dependants even if the trial ends in acquittal or discharge.
District Legal Services Authorities (DLSA) assess the amount of compensation under state schemes.
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) carries forward the victim compensation framework established under CrPC.

hindi_translation.headline: सुप्रीम कोर्ट का प्रस्ताव: आरोपी के बरी होने पर भी हत्या पीड़ित के परिवारों को मिले मुआवजा
hindi_translation.story_lead: उच्चतम न्यायालय ने प्रस्ताव दिया है कि अभियोजन पक्ष द्वारा संदेह से परे आरोप सिद्ध न कर पाने के कारण आरोपी के बरी होने की स्थिति में भी पीड़ित परिवारों को वित्तीय मुआवजा दिया जाना चाहिए। न्यायमूर्ति सतीश चंद्र शर्मा और न्यायमूर्ति एन कोटिश्वर सिंह की पीठ ने स्पष्ट किया कि आरोपी के बरी होने मात्र से पीड़ित परिवार को हुए नुकसान की अनदेखी नहीं की जानी चाहिए।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### पीड़ित मुआवजे पर सुप्रीम कोर्ट का प्रस्ताव
उच्चतम न्यायालय ने सुझाव दिया है कि पीड़ित मुआवजा योजनाओं को उन मामलों में भी लागू किया जाना चाहिए जहां पर्याप्त सबूत न होने के कारण अदालती कार्यवाही बरी होने पर समाप्त होती है। न्यायमूर्ति सतीश चंद्र शर्मा और न्यायमूर्ति एन कोटिश्वर सिंह की पीठ ने हरियाणा के 2011 के एक दोहरे हत्याकांड मामले में आरोपी को बरी करते हुए यह निर्देश जारी किया। अदालत ने भिवानी के जिला कानूनी सेवा प्राधिकरण (DLSA) को निर्देश दिया कि वह संबंधित कानूनी प्रावधानों की जांच करे और यह देखे कि क्या मृत महिलाओं के परिवारों को वित्तीय सहायता दी जा सकती है।

### 2011 हरियाणा दोहरे हत्याकांड की पृष्ठभूमि
यह मामला हरियाणा के भिवानी जिले के रानीला गांव में 17 अप्रैल 2011 को दो विधवा महिलाओं, शकुंतला और सुमन की हत्या से संबंधित है। अभियोजन पक्ष के अनुसार, व्यक्तिगत संबंधों के विवाद को लेकर दोनों महिलाओं की उनके भतीजे नरेश और एक अन्य व्यक्ति सुभाष द्वारा सार्वजनिक रूप से लाठियों से पीट-पीटकर हत्या कर दी गई थी। गिरफ्तारी के बाद 2013 में भिवानी की एक फास्ट-ट्रैक अदालत ने नरेश को दोषी ठहराते हुए मौत की सजा सुनाई थी।

### दोषमुक्ति और कानूनी सेवा प्राधिकरण को निर्देश
अपील की सुनवाई के दौरान सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने पाया कि आरोपी के खिलाफ सबूत संदेह से परे अपराध सिद्ध करने के लिए अपर्याप्त थे, जिसके बाद पीठ ने उसे बरी कर दिया। हालांकि, पीड़ित परिवारों के दर्द और नुकसान को देखते हुए पीठ ने कहा कि बरी होने से पीड़ित परिवार को राज्य सहायता से वंचित नहीं किया जाना चाहिए। यह निर्देश दंड प्रक्रिया संहिता (CrPC) की धारा 357A के तहत दिए गए हैं, जिसे भारतीय नागरिक सुरक्षा संहिता (BNSS) के तहत भी बरकरार रखा गया है।

news.exam_corner_topic: Three Major Shifts Shaping Modern Warfare Dynamics
static_gk: The post of Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) in India was officially created in December 2019 to serve as the principal military advisor to the Minister of Defence.
The CDS functions as the permanent Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee (COSC) and heads the Department of Military Affairs (DMA) within the Ministry of Defence.
news.headline: CDS General NS Raja Subramani Identifies Three Core Shifts Transforming Modern Warfare
news.story_lead: Speaking at the National Security Summit 3.0 in New Delhi, Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani highlighted three key shifts redefining future global conflicts. He emphasized the cost imbalance of modern weaponry, intense competition for critical technologies like AI and minerals, and the spatial expansion of battlefields beyond traditional frontlines.
news.full_article_text:
### Three Major Paradigm Shifts in Modern Warfare

Addressing the National Security Summit 3.0 organized by Asian News International (ANI) in New Delhi, Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) General NS Raja Subramani outlined the changing structural dynamics of modern military engagements. He identified three primary transformations that will shape strategic military planning and national defense readiness in the coming years:

#### 1. Economic Asymmetry in Warfare
General Subramani highlighted a sharp imbalance in the financial dynamics of contemporary conflict. He noted that utilizing interceptor missiles costing upwards of $1 million to neutralize unmanned aerial vehicles (drones) priced between $2,500 and $3,000 creates a heavy financial drain on defending forces. Citing the rapid expenditure rate of US Patriot air defense missiles during recent operations, he warned that replacing such sophisticated stockpiles can take years. He called for nations to prioritize manufacturing affordable, scalable, and readily available military hardware alongside high-end platforms.

#### 2. Contest for Technological Control
The second major trend is the heightened global rivalry for dominion over advanced technologies, notably Artificial Intelligence (AI), data infrastructure, and critical minerals. Pointing to the United States and China as the current frontrunners in technology, the CDS remarked that other nations are accelerating efforts to bridge this gap. He asserted that a nation's military and economic strength is fundamentally tied to its control over the critical technology powering its systems.

#### 3. Expansion of the Battle Space
The third transformation involves the dissolution of traditional geographic boundaries in war zone planning. Modern weapons and asymmetric platforms mean warfare is no longer confined to defined frontlines. The distinction between front positions and rear hinterlands has largely disappeared, rendering a nation's entire territory vulnerable. Essential civilian infrastructure—including power networks, data storage hubs, telecommunication grids, and urban centers—faces direct operational risk during military conflicts.

hindi_translation.headline: सीडीएस जनरल एनएस राजा सुब्रमणि ने आधुनिक युद्ध को आकार देने वाले तीन प्रमुख परिवर्तनों की पहचान की
hindi_translation.story_lead: नई दिल्ली में एएनआई के राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा शिखर सम्मेलन 3.0 को संबोधित करते हुए चीफ ऑफ डिफेंस स्टाफ जनरल एनएस राजा सुब्रमणि ने आधुनिक सैन्य रणनीति को प्रभावित करने वाले तीन प्रमुख बदलावों को रेखांकित किया। उन्होंने आधुनिक हथियारों के आर्थिक असंतुलन, एआई और महत्वपूर्ण खनिजों जैसी तकनीकों की प्रतिस्पर्धा और पारंपरिक सीमाओं से परे युद्धक्षेत्र के विस्तार पर जोर दिया।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### आधुनिक युद्ध में तीन प्रमुख परिवर्तन

नई दिल्ली में एशियन न्यूज इंटरनेशनल (एएनआई) द्वारा आयोजित नेशनल सिक्योरिटी समिट 3.0 को संबोधित करते हुए भारत के चीफ ऑफ डिफेंस स्टाफ (सीडीएस) जनरल एनएस राजा सुब्रमणि ने वैश्विक संघर्ष के बदलते स्वरूप पर अपने विचार रखे। उन्होंने तीन मुख्य परिवर्तनों की पहचान की जो आने वाले वर्षों में रक्षा योजनाओं और राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा की तैयारियों को तय करेंगे:

#### 1. युद्ध की बदलती आर्थिक गतिशीलता (आर्थिक असंतुलन)
जनरल सुब्रमणि ने आधुनिक संघर्ष में वित्तीय लागत के भारी असंतुलन को रेखांकित किया। उन्होंने उल्लेख किया कि $2,500 से $3,000 की कीमत वाले ड्रोन का मुकाबला करने के लिए $10 लाख (1 मिलियन डॉलर) की मिसाइलों का उपयोग करना रक्षा बलों के लिए गंभीर आर्थिक दबाव पैदा करता है। अमेरिकी पेट्रियट मिसाइल के स्टॉक में तेजी से आई कमी का उदाहरण देते हुए उन्होंने चेतावनी दी कि ऐसे उन्नत हथियारों की भरपाई में कई साल लग सकते हैं। उन्होंने कहा कि देशों को परिष्कृत हथियारों के साथ-साथ किफायती और बड़े पैमाने पर निर्मित होने वाले सैन्य उपकरणों का विकास करना होगा।

#### 2. तकनीकी वर्चस्व की होड़
दूसरा मुख्य बदलाव आर्टिफिशियल इंटेलिजेंस (एआई), डेटा प्रोसेसिंग और महत्वपूर्ण खनिजों (क्रिटिकल मिनरल्स) जैसे उन्नत क्षेत्रों पर नियंत्रण की अंतर्राष्ट्रीय प्रतिस्पर्धा है। अमेरिका और चीन को वर्तमान तकनीकी अग्रणी के रूप में चिन्हित करते हुए सीडीएस ने कहा कि अन्य देश भी इस अंतर को तेजी से पाटने में लगे हैं। उन्होंने जोर दिया कि किसी भी देश की आर्थिक और सैन्य ताकत उसकी महत्वपूर्ण तकनीकों पर पकड़ पर निर्भर करती है।

#### 3. युद्धक्षेत्र का भौगोलिक विस्तार
तीसरा बड़ा बदलाव पारंपरिक युद्ध क्षेत्रों का विस्तार है। आधुनिक हथियारों और तकनीकों के कारण युद्ध अब केवल मोर्चे तक सीमित नहीं रह गया है। मोर्चे और पिछले इलाकों (फ्रंट और रियर) के बीच का अंतर समाप्त हो चुका है। अब किसी देश का पूरा क्षेत्र संभावित युद्धक्षेत्र बन गया है। इसके परिणामस्वरूप देश के उद्योग, बिजली ग्रिड, संचार नेटवर्क, डेटा सेंटर और नागरिक भी सीधे हमलों के जोखिम में हैं।
bullet_points: सीडीएस जनरल एनएस राजा सुब्रमणि ने नई दिल्ली में एएनआई के नेशनल सिक्योरिटी समिट 3.0 को संबोधित किया।
$2,500-$3,000 के ड्रोन को नष्ट करने के लिए $10 लाख की मिसाइल के इस्तेमाल से उत्पन्न आर्थिक असंतुलन की चेतावनी दी।
अमेरिकी पेट्रियट मिसाइलों जैसे उन्नत हथियारों के तेजी से खत्म होने और उनकी पुनर्पूर्ति में सालों लगने का उल्लेख किया।
उन्नत प्रणालियों के साथ-साथ किफायती और बड़े पैमाने पर बनने वाले सैन्य उपकरणों के निर्माण की आवश्यकता पर बल दिया।
अमेरिका और चीन को एआई, डेटा और महत्वपूर्ण खनिजों के क्षेत्र में अग्रणी बताया।
चेतावनी दी कि मोर्चे और पिछले इलाकों के बीच का अंतर खत्म हो गया है और पूरा देश युद्धक्षेत्र के दायरे में है।

news.headline: Amazon Loses 40 Satellites Following Rocket Launch Failure Within 10 Minutes
news.story_lead: Amazon suffered a major setback in its satellite deployment plans after a rocket carrying 40 of its satellites failed within 10 minutes of liftoff. The mission failure resulted in the total loss of all 40 satellites aboard the launch vehicle.
news.full_article_text:
### Amazon Satellite Launch Failure

Amazon experienced a major operational setback after a rocket carrying 40 of its communications satellites suffered a failure shortly after liftoff, terminating the mission within 10 minutes. The incident led to the total loss of the 40 satellites being delivered into orbit.

- **Payload Details:** A total of 40 satellites owned by Amazon were onboard and destroyed.
- **Timeline of Anomaly:** The launch vehicle encountered a critical anomaly within 10 minutes of launch.
- **Significance:** The loss highlights technical vulnerabilities and concentrated financial risks associated with batch deployment of satellite constellations.
bullet_points: Amazon lost 40 satellites following a rocket launch failure.
The launch failure occurred within 10 minutes after liftoff.
The mission resulted in the complete destruction of all 40 satellites onboard.
The event underscores the technical risks inherent in satellite constellation launch operations.
key_facts: 40 Amazon satellites lost in mission failure.
Failure occurred within 10 minutes of rocket launch.
important_dates: 2026-11-16: Date of reported rocket launch failure carrying Amazon satellites
exam_relevance: Prelims: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations, satellite payloads, rocket launch phases, and propulsion systems.
Mains: Challenges in commercial space ventures, risk management in satellite deployment, and growth of space tech applications.
news.upsc_analysis: The loss of 40 satellites within ten minutes of launch highlights the high operational and capital risks linked with deploying megaconstellations in Low Earth Orbit (LEO). High-density payload launches require reliable space transportation systems to prevent major supply-chain and hardware setbacks.
causes: A mission anomaly occurring within 10 minutes of rocket liftoff leading to launch failure.
impacts: Destruction of 40 Amazon satellites.
Delay in Amazon's satellite constellation deployment timeline.
challenges: Ensuring high launch vehicle reliability for satellite batch deployments.
Managing financial and payload risk exposure during space launches.
way_forward: Conducting rigorous root-cause failure investigations to bolster future launch vehicle reliability and safeguard payload investments.
news.mains_notes:
### Satellite Megaconstellations & Launch Risks
- **Payload Concentration Risk:** Deploying large numbers of satellites in a single launch increases potential financial losses if launch vehicle anomalies occur.
- **LEO Infrastructure:** Building global satellite internet networks relies heavily on consistent and reliable space access capabilities.
mains_questions: Discuss the technical and economic risks associated with commercial satellite deployment in Low Earth Orbit (LEO).
Examine the critical role of launch vehicle reliability in the growth of the global private space industry.
news.takeaway: Amazon lost 40 satellites after a rocket launch failed within 10 minutes of liftoff.
prelims_facts: Amazon lost 40 satellites in a rocket launch failure.
The failure occurred within the first 10 minutes of flight.

news.full_article_text:
### Amazon Satellite Launch Anomaly

In a significant setback to commercial satellite constellation efforts, Amazon lost 40 satellites following a launch vehicle failure that occurred less than 10 minutes after liftoff. The mission ended in failure during the ascent phase, destroying all payload units on board.

#### Key Factual Details
* **Payload Loss:** A batch of 40 Amazon satellites was destroyed during the mission.
* **Failure Timeline:** An anomaly occurred within 10 minutes of launch, leading to mission failure.
* **Launch Partner:** The flight involved a United Launch Alliance (ULA) launch vehicle.
* **Publication Date:** November 16, 2026.

The entire payload of 40 satellites was destroyed before achieving orbit.
The launch involved a rocket provided by United Launch Alliance (ULA).
The incident impacts the deployment timeline for Amazon's satellite network.
Detailed investigations are expected to determine the exact technical anomaly causing the failure.

Time elapsed before launch failure: Under 10 minutes
Launch service provider involved: United Launch Alliance (ULA)
Entity owning the payload: Amazon

Financial and material losses for the satellite operator.

Mitigating risks of payload loss during initial launch ascent phases.
way_forward: Conducting root-cause analysis of the rocket launch failure to identify and rectify flight anomalies.
Implementing enhanced pre-flight checks and redundancy systems for future launch missions.
news.mains_notes:
### Commercial Space Operations & Launch Risks

* **Event Overview:** Amazon lost 40 satellites in a rocket launch failure that occurred within 10 minutes of launch.
* **Key Issues in Commercial Space:**
  1. **Launch Reliability:** High-density payload missions carry concentrated financial and operational risks during liftoff.

news.headline: CPI(M) demand judicial probe into 200 MW power purchase in Keralam
news.story_lead: CPI(M) demand judicial probe into 200 MW power purchase in Keralam Thiruvananthapuram, A judicial inquiry has been demanded into the procurement of 200 MW of electricity by the UDF government in October, amid allegations of large-scale corruption and a huge loss to the state exchequer. CPI state secretary M V Govindan alleged on Sunday that corruption had taken place in the deal, while Leader of Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan accused the government of purchasing power at a higher rate without following prescribed procedures. Speaking to reporters, Govindan said the electricity was procured at higher rates without inviting tenders or obtaining the necessary approvals from the Electricity Regulatory Commission and other authorities.
news.full_article_text: CPI(M) demand judicial probe into 200 MW power purchase in Keralam Thiruvananthapuram, A judicial inquiry has been demanded into the procurement of 200 MW of electricity by the UDF government in October, amid allegations of large-scale corruption and a huge loss to the state exchequer. CPI state secretary M V Govindan alleged on Sunday that corruption had taken place in the deal, while Leader of Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan accused the government of purchasing power at a higher rate without following prescribed procedures. Speaking to reporters, Govindan said the electricity was procured at higher rates without inviting tenders or obtaining the necessary approvals from the Electricity Regulatory Commission and other authorities. The purchase was made under emergency provisions without proper consultation, he said. "This is a serious and dangerous development. All files related to the procurement should be made available to the public to ensure transparency," he said. He referred to differences between the electricity minister and the chief minister over the issue, which, he said, had become public. Demanding a judicial inquiry, Govindan said the chief minister was involved in the decision-making process and that an independent investigation was necessary to bring out the facts. In a Facebook post, Vijayan alleged that the government had purchased 200 MW of electricity from VEH Global at ₹ 11 per unit without a tender or approval from the commission. He said he had raised allegations of corruption in the deal in a statement on November 10 and that further details had since emerged. Under Sections 62 and 63 of the Electricity Act, power procurement prices must be determined through procedures approved by the commission or through competitive bidding, Vijayan said. However, the decision to purchase electricity from VEH Global in October was based solely on offers, and the commission had not yet approved the arrangement, he alleged. He pointed out that wind power was available at ₹ 3-4 per unit, while the government had agreed to purchase electricity at ₹ 11 per unit, resulting in a huge loss to the exchequer. Vijayan said the government had accepted VEH Global's offer to supply electricity during peak hours on September 22. He alleged that the government's earlier orders had stated that the company was not eligible to participate in the tender for electricity supply. "Who was interested in awarding the contract to a company that was not eligible?" he asked. He demanded that the chief minister give the public a clear explanation of the alleged irregularities. news.headline: Bengal BJP leader dies after alleged assault by party workers in Panihati: Cop
news.story_lead: Bengal BJP leader dies after alleged assault by party workers in Panihati: Cop The incident comes amid repeated warnings from senior BJP leaders and ministers that party workers and leaders involved in organised crime A local Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader died in West Bengal’s North 24 Parganas district on Saturday night after he was allegedly assaulted by members of a rival group within the party when he intervened in a dispute involving his wife, police said. Arup Saha, the husband of BJP’s local mandal (unit) secretary Ruma Saha, was allegedly assaulted after he came to her rescue during an altercation with a group of party workers in Panihati. Ruma had intervened when the group allegedly assaulted a local trader, Shankar Dey.
news.full_article_text: Bengal BJP leader dies after alleged assault by party workers in Panihati: Cop The incident comes amid repeated warnings from senior BJP leaders and ministers that party workers and leaders involved in organised crime A local Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader died in West Bengal’s North 24 Parganas district on Saturday night after he was allegedly assaulted by members of a rival group within the party when he intervened in a dispute involving his wife, police said. Arup Saha, the husband of BJP’s local mandal (unit) secretary Ruma Saha, was allegedly assaulted after he came to her rescue during an altercation with a group of party workers in Panihati. Ruma had intervened when the group allegedly assaulted a local trader, Shankar Dey. Arup later complained of chest pain and was taken to Sagar Dutta Medical College and Hospital, where he died, his wife said. “Arup Saha, the deceased, was the husband of the BJP’s local mandal secretary Ruma Saha. People are alleging that Arup went to rescue his wife when she was verbally abused by rival group members for trying to save a trader from their assault. Nobody, however, lodged any complaint till Sunday morning,” a district police officer said, requesting anonymity. Ruma Saha said she intervened after hearing that followers of a BJP youth wing leader were assaulting the trader. “I went to the rescue of a trader when I heard that followers of a BJP youth wing leader were assaulting him. These people surrounded me and verbally abused me. They hit my husband when he intervened. He complained of chest pain after we returned home and died at Sagar Dutta Medical College and Hospital,” she said. Shankar Dey said, “I fell on the ground when they hit me. The BJP workers surrounded Ruma Saha when she tried to stop them.” Ruma Saha alleged that the assailants were followers of Nirmal Ghosh, a former Trinamool Congress MLA from Panihati who faces multiple criminal charges and was recently released on bail. Ghosh is also an accused in the rape and murder case involving the daughter of BJP MLA Ratna Debnath at RG Kar Medical College and Hospital in 2024. Ghosh could not be contacted despite several attempts. Debnath, who won the Panihati assembly seat for the BJP in May, told the media that “unwanted elements” continued to operate within the party despite repeated warnings. “I earlier requested the government to intervene. Politicians involved in illegal activities during the Trinamool Congress regime are still active in Panihati,” she said. The incident comes amid repeated warnings from senior BJP leaders and ministers that party workers and leaders involved in organised crime, including extortion, would face action. State BJP leaders have also alleged that Trinamool Congress leaders and their followers who joined the BJP after the assembly elections on May 4 continued to engage in extortion and intra-party violence. West Bengal finance minister Swapan Dasgupta admitted on Saturday that extortion continued under the BJP government. “Extortion is like the new normal. People’s confidence in the administration cannot be restored until it ends. I have stopped some extortions in my constituency but we have not been able to end it fully,” Dasgupta said. On Friday, BJP state president Samik Bhattacharya issued a warning at an event organised by the party’s women’s wing. He alleged that some police personnel were tacitly supporting illegal activities. “Some (BJP) mandal presidents are thinking they are the police and some police personnel are thinking they are the mandal presidents. No lawlessness will be allowed. Identify those who are tarnishing the party and its flag and file FIRs (first information reports). “Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari is also in charge of the police department. I am there too. Give me the papers and I will ensure that these people land in jail,” Bhattacharya said. The Trinamool Congress said Bhattacharya might have good intentions but the law and order situation had deteriorated under the BJP government. Kalyan Banerjee, a senior lawyer and five-time Trinamool Congress Lok Sabha MP from Sreerampur in Hooghly district, questioned how complaints could be registered if the police refused to accept them. “Samik may have good intentions but how can an FIR be filed if the police do not accept complaints?” he said. “I can cite an instance from Sreerampur. A woman was molested by BJP workers who also extorted money from her, but the police told her that it was impossible for them to register her complaint,” Banerjee alleged. In a separate incident on Saturday, Koustav Bagchi, the BJP MLA from Barrackpore in North 24 Parganas district, had two people arrested for allegedly selling domestic LPG cylinders illegally in his constituency. “People who ran illegal businesses and gambling dens in Barrackpore during the Trinamool regime are still active,” Bagchi said after facing a demonstration by some BJP workers.

Taking a swipe at the BJP, he said those who have considered Agra their stronghold would soon lose their foothold. "Looking at the support of the Dalit community, I can say that the 'D' in our 'PDA', has now become 'Damdar Dalit'," he said. Yadav claimed the BJP is conspiring against the 'PDA' after its electoral defeat in the recent bypolls. He further alleged that around 200 statues of Dr B R Ambedkar had been vandalised in the state over the past decade. "No action has been taken against those responsible." Yadav said the Samajwadi Party has published a newsletter documenting such incidents of vandalism, including details of where they took place and those allegedly responsible. "Those who vandalise Dr Ambedkar's statues do not merely attack the sculpture. They attack the Constitution held in Babasaheb's hand," he said. "If there is a Constitution, there is dignity. If there is a Constitution, there are rights. If there is a Constitution, there is democracy. And it is democracy that keeps the Constitution alive," he asserted, alleging the BJP's allegiance to "Man Vidhan (anarchy)" instead of the 'Samvidhan' (Constitution). Yadav claimed that the massive turnout at the event reflected growing support for the party's political campaign. He also questioned the claims of the "double-engine" government. "Those who used to talk about double-engine government have been handed a double zero in Kashi," he said, referring to the loss of the BJP candidate from Varanasi in the recent legislative council election. Taking a swipe at Union Home Minister Amit Shah 's recent remarks likening the BJP government in Uttar Pradesh to "Angad ka paon (Angad's foot)", an idiom for immovable, Yadav said the ruling party would soon lose its "footing". "Those who are saying that this government is 'Angad ka paon' will lose their footing. When there is no ground left, where will they place 'Angad ka paon'?" he said. In an apparent jibe at AIMIM chief and Hyderabad MP Asaduddin Owaisi, Yadav said some "political tourists" have started arriving in Uttar Pradesh after the BJP's electoral defeats in assembly bypolls and legislative council elections. He further alleged that the political strings of these leaders are controlled from elsewhere, in an apparent reference to Owaisi-led All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen's recent alliance with Nagina MP Chandra Shekhar Aazad's Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram) ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. "Since the BJP lost, I see several political tourists arriving. They have become loudspeakers for someone else's microphone," he said. Referring to the recent Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council elections, Yadav hailed the victory of Samajwadi Party-backed Akash Agarwal from Agra, alleging that the entire administrative machinery was employed to defeat the candidate. Agarwal was humiliated and subjected to the worst of abuses, but he still emerged victorious, he said, asserting that those who have faced injustice and humiliation are the strength of the 'PDA'. Accusing the BJP government of playing with the future of young people, Yadav claimed that question papers of more than 20 public examinations had been leaked in Uttar Pradesh, leading to their cancellation. He alleged that the government was bent on depriving the youth of employment and reservation opportunities. Yadav also claimed that the BJP government had shut down 26,000 primary schools where children from poor and Dalit families studied. "The government is shutting down schools and opening liquor shops," he jibed, adding that the closures had also affected government teaching jobs. Raising the issue of representation in higher education institutions, Yadav alleged that Dalits and backward classes were not getting adequate opportunities in these institutions. He also criticised the condition of government hospitals, claiming that patients were referred to private hospitals when they failed to receive treatment at government facilities. Yadav alleged that crimes against women, too, were on the rise under BJP rule. He said a Samajwadi Party government would establish the rule of law and ensure social justice. It would also improve the police and emergency response mechanisms to ensure timely justice for the poor. Describing the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections as a contest between five per cent and 95 per cent of the population, Yadav alleged that the BJP had exacerbated people's suffering over the past decade. Referring to the agitation by candidates during the ongoing assistant teachers' recruitment drive over reservation, he said a Samajwadi Party government would ensure that they received their due. "This time, the lathi will lose and the laptop will win. The youth want to study and progress, but attempts are being made to intimidate them," he said.

news.headline: Missing for 15 days, Odisha teacher found alive in ravine after goat herder hears cries
news.story_lead: Missing for 15 days, Odisha teacher found alive in ravine after goat herder hears cries After he went missing, his family approached Raikia police station, where a missing-person complaint was lodged on November 5 Trapped in a forest ravine and cut off from the outside world, a 47-year-old primary school teacher in Odisha’s Kandhamal district survived for nearly a fortnight on muddy rainwater and whatever edible food he could find. He was rescued on Saturday after a young goat herder heard his faint cries for help while grazing his animals in the forest. Mohan Kumar Maharana, a teacher at Sarsapeta Primary School in the Duba area of Kandhamal, had been missing for 15 days after heavy rainfall and a massive landslide triggered by Cyclone Arnab on October 29.
news.full_article_text: Missing for 15 days, Odisha teacher found alive in ravine after goat herder hears cries After he went missing, his family approached Raikia police station, where a missing-person complaint was lodged on November 5 Trapped in a forest ravine and cut off from the outside world, a 47-year-old primary school teacher in Odisha’s Kandhamal district survived for nearly a fortnight on muddy rainwater and whatever edible food he could find. He was rescued on Saturday after a young goat herder heard his faint cries for help while grazing his animals in the forest. Mohan Kumar Maharana, a teacher at Sarsapeta Primary School in the Duba area of Kandhamal, had been missing for 15 days after heavy rainfall and a massive landslide triggered by Cyclone Arnab on October 29. He was returning from school when the landslide struck near Dangesi village, trapping him in the forested hillside. “As a young goat herder had ventured into the forest with his animals, he heard a faint voice coming from the area. On approaching the spot, he found Maharana lying in an extremely weak condition on a rock inside the ravine. The herder immediately alerted the villagers and police,” said Raikia police station officer-in-charge A Swarnalata Patra, who led the rescue operation along with police personnel and local villagers. As the hillside gave way near Dangesi village, residents fled towards safer locations, but Maharana became separated from the others. In the darkness and confusion, he slipped into a deep ditch or ravine. With no one around to hear his cries for help, he remained stranded in the forest, unable to find a way out. Continuous rainfall, flooding and the absence of mobile network connectivity in the area compounded his ordeal. His cries gradually weakened as hunger and exhaustion took their toll. Maharana’s wife said her husband struggled to survive in the forest for several days. “He drank muddy water collected in the ditch and from nearby streams to quench his thirst. He also managed to eat whatever edible things he could find in the forest. At one stage, he became so physically weak that he could no longer attempt to escape,” she said. After he went missing, his family approached Raikia police station, where a missing-person complaint was lodged on November 5. Police also alerted residents of neighbouring villages, asking them to report any information about the teacher. “We tried calling him on his mobile phone but knew it would be futile, considering the area has patchy mobile network coverage and his phone would have run out of battery in the rain,” his wife said. Although the goat herder found Maharana, bringing him out of the ravine was a formidable challenge. Rescuers had to trek nearly seven to eight kilometres through dense forest and difficult hilly terrain. They eventually carried him out on a makeshift stretcher fashioned from a wooden pole and a bedsheet. Maharana was taken to Raikia Community Health Centre for treatment. Doctors said prolonged starvation and physical exhaustion had left him extremely weak. He had also suffered cuts and other injuries during the ordeal. His family demanded that he be shifted to Phulbani Medical College and Hospital for better treatment. Officials said Cyclone Arnab and the subsequent landslide had disrupted normal life in Raikia, with residents of affected villages evacuated to government relief shelters, including one at Manikeshwar. “With the school closed and villagers moved to safer locations, the forested surroundings remained largely deserted, which is why no one could find him for so long,” Patra said. The landslide near Dangesi also killed three members of a family, including a nine-month-old boy, when their hilltop house was buried under debris. In neighbouring Ganjam district, Cyclone Arnab triggered another landslide in Gidipabali village, where five bodies were recovered after an extensive search. The district administration on Monday suspended search and rescue operations after families of six missing persons submitted written requests asking officials to stop the operation. They said their houses and family members could be buried under massive rocks and debris at an estimated depth of around 30 feet. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Debabrata Mohanty Debabrata Mohanty is a senior assistant editor of Hindustan Times who works as state correspondent from Odisha covering the state's politics, governance, public policy, natural disasters, environment and its society for close to three decades. With his long years of reporting from the state capital of Bhubaneswar, Mohanty has been known as one of the most experienced and credible journalists covering Odisha for the national English dailies. His reporting combines on-ground detail with deep institutional knowledge detailing the state's changing politics, governance issues, administrative reforms and the functioning of its public institutions. He has regularly reported on issues ranging from legislative developments and public policy implementation. Politics is his core areas of expertise as he closely tracks Odisha's political landscape, including the rise and transformation of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the Biju Janata Dal (BJD), the two principal political parties in Odisha. His long association with the state's political establishment enables him to write on contemporary developments in a larger political context. Mohanty takes a deep interest in writing human interest stories, environmental issues and documenting the impact of cyclones, floods, heatwaves, and other climate-related events in one of the most disaster-prone states. His coverage extends to public health, governance reforms and stories on accountability of government institutions. Before joining Hindustan Times, Mohanty worked with The Indian Express, Mail Today, and The Telegraph, where he covered at least six general elections and as many assembly elections. In 2007, he was selected for the prestigious Chevening Young Indian Print Journalist Programme at the University of Lincoln, United Kingdom, where he received advanced training in print journalism. In 2009 he won the Press Institute of India-International Committee of Red Cross award on conflict reporting for his on-ground reportage of 2008 Kandhamal riots. Read More

Trapped in a forest ravine and cut off from the outside world, a 47-year-old primary school teacher in Odisha’s Kandhamal district survived for nearly a fortnight on muddy rainwater and whatever edible food he could find. He was rescued on Saturday after a young goat herder heard his faint cries for help while grazing his animals in the forest.

Mohan Kumar Maharana, a teacher at Sarsapeta Primary School in the Duba area of Kandhamal, had been missing for 15 days after heavy rainfall and a massive landslide triggered by Cyclone Arnab on October 29. He was returning from school when the landslide struck near Dangesi village, trapping him in the forested hillside.

“As a young goat herder had ventured into the forest with his animals, he heard a faint voice coming from the area. On approaching the spot, he found Maharana lying in an extremely weak condition on a rock inside the ravine. The herder immediately alerted the villagers and police,” said Raikia police station officer-in-charge A Swarnalata Patra, who led the rescue operation along with police personnel and local villagers.

As the hillside gave way near Dangesi village, residents fled towards safer locations, but Maharana became separated from the others. In the darkness and confusion, he slipped into a deep ditch or ravine. With no one around to hear his cries for help, he remained stranded in the forest, unable to find a way out.

He was rescued on Saturday after a young goat herder heard his faint cries for help while grazing his animals in the forest. Mohan Kumar Maharana, a teacher at Sarsapeta Primary School in the Duba area of Kandhamal, had been missing for 15 days after heavy rainfall and a massive landslide triggered by Cyclone Arnab on October 29. He was returning from school when the landslide struck near Dangesi village, trapping him in the forested hillside. “As a young goat herder had ventured into the forest with his animals, he heard a faint voice coming from the area. On approaching the spot, he found Maharana lying in an extremely weak condition on a rock inside the ravine. The herder immediately alerted the villagers and police,” said Raikia police station officer-in-charge A Swarnalata Patra, who led the rescue operation along with police personnel and local villagers. As the hillside gave way near Dangesi village, residents fled towards safer locations, but Maharana became separated from the others. In the darkness and confusion, he slipped into a deep ditch or ravine. With no one around to hear his cries for help, he remained stranded in the forest, unable to find a way out. Continuous rainfall, flooding and the absence of mobile network connectivity in the area compounded his ordeal. His cries gradually weakened as hunger and exhaustion took their toll. Maharana’s wife said her husband struggled to survive in the forest for several days. “He drank muddy water collected in the ditch and from nearby streams to quench his thirst. He also managed to eat whatever edible things he could find in the forest. At one stage, he became so physically weak that he could no longer attempt to escape,” she said. After he went missing, his family approached Raikia police station, where a missing-person complaint was lodged on November 5. Police also alerted residents of neighbouring villages, asking them to report any information about the teacher. “We tried calling him on his mobile phone but knew it would be futile, considering the area has patchy mobile network coverage and his phone would have run out of battery in the rain,” his wife said. Although the goat herder found Maharana, bringing him out of the ravine was a formidable challenge. Rescuers had to trek nearly seven to eight kilometres through dense forest and difficult hilly terrain. They eventually carried him out on a makeshift stretcher fashioned from a wooden pole and a bedsheet. Maharana was taken to Raikia Community Health Centre for treatment. Doctors said prolonged starvation and physical exhaustion had left him extremely weak. He had also suffered cuts and other injuries during the ordeal. His family demanded that he be shifted to Phulbani Medical College and Hospital for better treatment. Officials said Cyclone Arnab and the subsequent landslide had disrupted normal life in Raikia, with residents of affected villages evacuated to government relief shelters, including one at Manikeshwar. “With the school closed and villagers moved to safer locations, the forested surroundings remained largely deserted, which is why no one could find him for so long,” Patra said. The landslide near Dangesi also killed three members of a family, including a nine-month-old boy, when their hilltop house was buried under debris. In neighbouring Ganjam district, Cyclone Arnab triggered another landslide in Gidipabali village, where five bodies were recovered after an extensive search. The district administration on Monday suspended search and rescue operations after families of six missing persons submitted written requests asking officials to stop the operation. They said their houses and family members could be buried under massive rocks and debris at an estimated depth of around 30 feet. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Debabrata Mohanty Debabrata Mohanty is a senior assistant editor of Hindustan Times who works as state correspondent from Odisha covering the state's politics, governance, public policy, natural disasters, environment and its society for close to three decades. With his long years of reporting from the state capital of Bhubaneswar, Mohanty has been known as one of the most experienced and credible journalists covering Odisha for the national English dailies. His reporting combines on-ground detail with deep institutional knowledge detailing the state's changing politics, governance issues, administrative reforms and the functioning of its public institutions. He has regularly reported on issues ranging from legislative developments and public policy implementation. Politics is his core areas of expertise as he closely tracks Odisha's political landscape, including the rise and transformation of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the Biju Janata Dal (BJD), the two principal political parties in Odisha. His long association with the state's political establishment enables him to write on contemporary developments in a larger political context. Mohanty takes a deep interest in writing human interest stories, environmental issues and documenting the impact of cyclones, floods, heatwaves, and other climate-related events in one of the most disaster-prone states. His coverage extends to public health, governance reforms and stories on accountability of government institutions. Before joining Hindustan Times, Mohanty worked with The Indian Express, Mail Today, and The Telegraph, where he covered at least six general elections and as many assembly elections. In 2007, he was selected for the prestigious Chevening Young Indian Print Journalist Programme at the University of Lincoln, United Kingdom, where he received advanced training in print journalism. In 2009 he won the Press Institute of India-International Committee of Red Cross award on conflict reporting for his on-ground reportage of 2008 Kandhamal riots. Read More

news.headline: Bengal police shoots dead ‘criminal’ who allegedly opened fire at cop two days ago; fifth encounter in 6 months
news.story_lead: Bengal police shoots dead ‘criminal’ who allegedly opened fire at cop two days ago; fifth encounter in 6 months Criminal Ratan Sheikh was charged 36 criminal cases in Bengal's Birbhum district and had opene dfire at a police constable two days ago. A history sheeter in Bengal's Birbhum district was killed in a police encounter on Sunday afternoon, police said. The deceased has been identified as Ratan Sheikh and had allegedly opened fire and injured a police constable two days ago while police tried to arrest him shortly after his release on bail in one of the cases, district police officers said.
news.full_article_text: Bengal police shoots dead ‘criminal’ who allegedly opened fire at cop two days ago; fifth encounter in 6 months Criminal Ratan Sheikh was charged 36 criminal cases in Bengal's Birbhum district and had opene dfire at a police constable two days ago. A history sheeter in Bengal's Birbhum district was killed in a police encounter on Sunday afternoon, police said. The deceased has been identified as Ratan Sheikh and had allegedly opened fire and injured a police constable two days ago while police tried to arrest him shortly after his release on bail in one of the cases, district police officers said. Sheikh was charged in 36 criminal cases, police said. "Ratan Sheikh, a man with a long criminal history, was found during a manhunt ordered by chief minister Suvendu Adhikari who visited the injured constable, Biswajit Das, at the Burdwan Medical College and Hospital on Saturday," a Birbhum district police officer said, requesting anonymity. Also read: BJP targets Rahul Gandhi after Italian leader raises 'vote chor' slogan: 'Who laughs when India is insulted' A second officer, requesting anonymity, said that police traced Sheikh on Sunday and interrogated him to locate the pistol he used on Saturday. He led the police to Nanoor where the pistol was kept near a bridge but suddenly opened fire with it. The officer said, "The bullets hit a police vehicle. The police team returned fire in self-defence and Sheikh was hit." Doctors at Bolpur subdivisional hospital declared Sheikh dead and his body was taken to the morgue. Sheikh is the fifth criminal to have been killed in a police encounter in West Bengal since the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) came to power in May. Of the four men who died earlier, three were accused in rape and murder of minor girls, while one was the prime suspect in the murder of a BJP worker. Also read: Property dispute, gold sale among suspected motives behind serial murders by Bengaluru cab driver The Birbhum district police did not make any official statement on Sheikh's death till 7 pm. Constable Biswajit Das was shot in the leg during a raid at the Layekbazar bus stand in the Santiniketan police station area of Bolpur on Friday when he went there to arrest Sheikh in connection with one of the 36 cases.

news.headline: Punjab Congress forms panel to oversee induction of leaders from other parties
news.story_lead: Punjab Congress forms panel to oversee induction of leaders from other parties The induction process shall be carried forward only after taking their views into consideration, ensuring proper coordination with the local leadership. Ahead of next year's Assembly elections, Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh on Sunday formed a four-member committee to oversee and coordinate the induction of leaders from other parties. The four members include ex-MLA and Congress Working Committee member Vijay Inder Singla, MLA and deputy leader of the Congress Legislature Party (CLP) in the Assembly, Aruna Chaudhary, former MLA Kushaldeep Singh Dhillon and MLA Hardev Singh Laddi.
news.full_article_text: Punjab Congress forms panel to oversee induction of leaders from other parties The induction process shall be carried forward only after taking their views into consideration, ensuring proper coordination with the local leadership. Ahead of next year's Assembly elections, Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh on Sunday formed a four-member committee to oversee and coordinate the induction of leaders from other parties. The four members include ex-MLA and Congress Working Committee member Vijay Inder Singla, MLA and deputy leader of the Congress Legislature Party (CLP) in the Assembly, Aruna Chaudhary, former MLA Kushaldeep Singh Dhillon and MLA Hardev Singh Laddi. The committee will ensure that before any leader is inducted into the Congress, due consultations are held with the senior leaders of the concerned area and the respective district Congress presidents, a party statement said. The induction process shall be carried forward only after taking their views into consideration, ensuring proper coordination with the local leadership, it said. Elections to the 117-member Punjab Assembly are due early next year.

news.headline: Assam to restrict construction in flood-prone areas under proposed zoning law: CM
news.story_lead: Assam to restrict construction in flood-prone areas under proposed zoning law: CM The state government has prepared the Assam Flood Plain Zoning Bill, 2026, which will be tabled during the winter session of the state assembly next month The Assam government plans to bring the floodplains of the Brahmaputra and Barak river basins under a legal land-use zoning system to restrict and regulate construction in vulnerable areas, Chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said on Sunday. The move aims to address the risks posed by unregulated development in flood-prone areas. The state government has prepared the Assam Flood Plain Zoning Bill, 2026, which will be tabled during the winter session of the state assembly next month.
news.full_article_text: Assam to restrict construction in flood-prone areas under proposed zoning law: CM The state government has prepared the Assam Flood Plain Zoning Bill, 2026, which will be tabled during the winter session of the state assembly next month The Assam government plans to bring the floodplains of the Brahmaputra and Barak river basins under a legal land-use zoning system to restrict and regulate construction in vulnerable areas, Chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said on Sunday. The move aims to address the risks posed by unregulated development in flood-prone areas. The state government has prepared the Assam Flood Plain Zoning Bill, 2026, which will be tabled during the winter session of the state assembly next month. Sarma wrote on X: “Flood management begins with understanding our rivers. The Assam Flood Plain Zoning Bill, 2026, provides for scientific mapping of the Brahmaputra and Barak basins and clearly defined flood zones to protect communities and guide safer development.” The proposed legislation envisages using LiDAR technology and satellite imagery to map flood-prone areas across the two river basins. Based on this mapping, the government plans to classify land into three categories: prohibited, regulated and unregulated, with different restrictions on construction and development in each zone. River channels and areas of active flow would fall under the prohibited zone, where construction would not be allowed. Development in regulated zones would be subject to conditions such as elevated plinths and flood-resilient building designs, while normal development would be permitted in unregulated areas outside the identified flood lines. The proposed zoning system would add a land-use regulation mechanism to the state’s existing flood-control measures, which include embankments, riverbank protection, river-training works and drainage improvements. While these measures seek to protect settlements and infrastructure from floodwaters and erosion, the proposed law aims to regulate construction in areas exposed to flooding. Floodplain zoning has featured in Assam’s disaster-management planning before. The Assam State Disaster Management Plan, 2022, called for a regulatory framework to demarcate vulnerable areas and manage construction in floodplains. The proposed Bill seeks to give that planning a legal framework. The draft also envisages setting up Flood Zoning Authorities at different administrative levels to oversee its implementation. During a review of the draft on November 5, Sarma directed officials to ensure that lawful existing property owners were protected. He also stressed the need to safeguard the interests of Scheduled Tribe and Scheduled Caste communities traditionally residing along riverbanks. The proposed framework provides for a 60-day period for public hearings and objections, as well as online and physical mechanisms to appeal against zoning decisions. It also includes safeguards for existing property owners. The need for a broader approach to flood management has been underlined by the scale of this year’s floods. According to the state government’s November 5 review, floods in Sivasagar, Charaideo, Jorhat and Golaghat in July claimed 104 lives. The government has said the initiative could be financed through externally aided projects and grants, without imposing an additional financial burden on the state. Sarma has also expressed hope of securing central assistance, including through the Union ministry of Jal Shakti.

news.headline: Rajasthan teacher arrested after refusing to marry 61-year-old Canadian woman he met on dating app
news.story_lead: Rajasthan teacher arrested after refusing to marry 61-year-old Canadian woman he met on dating app Two days after the woman's arrival, the teacher told her he would not go ahead with the marriage because of their age difference A 31-year-old school teacher was arrested in Rajasthan’s Neemrana after he refused to marry a 61-year-old Canadian woman he had met on a dating app, police said. The woman had travelled to India for the wedding on November 11. Two days after her arrival, the teacher told her he would not go ahead with the marriage because of their age difference, an officer familiar with the case told HT.
news.full_article_text: Rajasthan teacher arrested after refusing to marry 61-year-old Canadian woman he met on dating app Two days after the woman's arrival, the teacher told her he would not go ahead with the marriage because of their age difference A 31-year-old school teacher was arrested in Rajasthan’s Neemrana after he refused to marry a 61-year-old Canadian woman he had met on a dating app, police said. The woman had travelled to India for the wedding on November 11. Two days after her arrival, the teacher told her he would not go ahead with the marriage because of their age difference, an officer familiar with the case told HT. Also read | Punjab woman, accomplice held in Rajasthan train track blast; police suspect ISI's 'romance' strategy to recruit women On Friday, November 13, the woman contacted the Canadian High Commission after the two argued. Officials alerted Neemrana police, who went to the flat where the pair were staying and took them to the police station. “Had agreed to marry” Neemrana station house officer Surendra Yadav identified the teacher as Nitin, who works at a private school in Panipat, Haryana. “Nitin and the woman began speaking on the app about a year ago. They grew close and had agreed to marry before she made the trip,” Yadav said. Also read | Rajasthan police bust interstate extortion, digital arrest gang; 4 women among 6 held The woman arrived in India on a tourist visa, Yadav said. “Nitin met her at Delhi airport on Wednesday and took her to his relatives’ flat in Neemrana,” he said. When she brought up their wedding plans at the flat, Nitin refused to marry her and the two argued, he added. Yadav said the teacher was arrested for breach of the peace and later released on bail. The woman underwent a medical examination and was taken to a care centre in Kotputli. She was later sent back to the Canadian High Commission in New Delhi. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR HT News Desk Follow the latest breaking news, major developments and agenda-setting stories from India and around the world with the newsdesk at Hindustan Times. news.headline: Punjab woman, accomplice held in Rajasthan train track blast; police suspect ISI's 'romance' strategy to recruit women
news.story_lead: Punjab woman, accomplice held in Rajasthan train track blast; police suspect ISI's 'romance' strategy to recruit women Police said the woman is a resident of Gurdaspur and is separated from her husband who is lodged in jail in Punjab in a drug trafficking case. A day after a woman and her male accomplice were arrested from Gurdaspur in Punjab in connection with the November 3 railway track blast in Sri Ganganagar, Rajasthan, police on Sunday said that the accused had links with Pakistan-based handlers and had made two unsuccessful attempts to blow up the railway line before carrying out the explosion earlier this month. The 21-year-old woman and her 23-year-old male accomplice were arrested on Saturday in a joint operation by the Rajasthan Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS), Sri Ganganagar Police and Punjab Police.
news.full_article_text: Punjab woman, accomplice held in Rajasthan train track blast; police suspect ISI's 'romance' strategy to recruit women Police said the woman is a resident of Gurdaspur and is separated from her husband who is lodged in jail in Punjab in a drug trafficking case. A day after a woman and her male accomplice were arrested from Gurdaspur in Punjab in connection with the November 3 railway track blast in Sri Ganganagar, Rajasthan, police on Sunday said that the accused had links with Pakistan-based handlers and had made two unsuccessful attempts to blow up the railway line before carrying out the explosion earlier this month. The 21-year-old woman and her 23-year-old male accomplice were arrested on Saturday in a joint operation by the Rajasthan Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS), Sri Ganganagar Police and Punjab Police. Also read: Bengal police shoot dead ‘criminal’ who allegedly opened fire at cop two days ago; fifth encounter in 6 months Investigators recovered two foreign-made pistols, 46 live cartridges and ₹ 30,000 allegedly received for carrying out the blast, police said. Alleged Pak handlers linked to ISI ATS Additional Director General of Police Dinesh MN said preliminary investigations revealed that the duo was in contact with two Pakistan-based handlers, identified as Shah and Chacha, the latter suspected of having links with Pakistan's Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI). "The woman was in contact with Pakistani handler Shah and carried out the blast with the assistance of her accomplice. They were acting on instructions from Shah and another person known as Chacha in Pakistan, who is suspected to be associated with the ISI," Dinesh said. Also read: BJP targets Rahul Gandhi after Italian leader raises 'vote chor' slogan: 'Who laughs when India is insulted' Police said the woman is a resident of Dostpur village in Gurdaspur and is separated from her husband who is lodged in jail in Punjab in a drug trafficking case. Investigators suspect she subsequently established contact with Pakistan-based handlers. She had allegedly been in contact with the handlers for nearly 15 months and had been communicating with them primarily through WhatsApp. Police said the accused initially planned to target the railway track in the Ramsinghpur police station area on October 6, but the attempt could not proceed because explosives were unavailable. On October 12 or 13, they allegedly planted a timer bomb supplied by Shah, but it failed to explode due to a technical malfunction. The third attempt, on November 3, resulted in the explosion around 9.45 pm. Investigators believe the prime suspect was chosen for the operation because her presence near the railway track was less likely to create suspicion. How the arrests were carried out The arrests followed technical surveillance, examination of social media accounts and intelligence inputs from central agencies. A team led by IPS officer Nitin Chaudhary and ATS Bikaner unit in-charge Surendra Kumar coordinated with Punjab Counter Intelligence and Gurdaspur SSP Aditya to apprehend the suspects.
